audience.programmeDescription: Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Groningen is taught in Dutch and examines the region’s history, politics, cultures and religious traditions. Students learn Arabic, complete a minor and write a thesis. The standard second-year curriculum includes a semester in Cairo or Rabat.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR courses explore empires, Mediterranean art and literature alongside comparative politics and international relations. Groningen offers sustained study of modern Middle Eastern societies, regional politics and religious traditions. The table shows Groningen’s curriculum.

componentNotes.mes-y1-faculty-wide: Choose a faculty-wide course on Global Change or Cultural Heritage.
componentNotes.mes-y2-arabic-advanced: Students must pass the beginner and intermediate Arabic courses before starting this course.
componentNotes.mes-y2-study-abroad: The standard 30 EC semester is in Cairo or Rabat. Entry requires 45 EC from year one and completion of Advanced Arabic. Groningen permits deviations in exceptional circumstances.
componentNotes.mes-y3-thesis: Complete all 60 first-year credits before starting. The thesis normally takes place in the second semester.
componentNotes.mes-y3-faculty-wide: Choose a faculty-wide course on Global Change or Cultural Heritage.
